title: Staff of the Board and the Mayor’s office: where they came from and went
question: Who worked as a supervisor’s aide or on the Mayor’s staff, and what do the files show about where they came from and where they went?
finding: The payroll names 178 legislative aides at the Board of Supervisors and 204 Mayoral staff between fiscal 2017 and 2026 (names that behave as one person). The Clerk’s Board Roster and the supervisors’ own pages (2026) tie 45 current staff to 12 offices, 33 of whom are found on the payroll; with campaign payments and filings that name an aide as an official’s contact, 62 of the payroll’s aides and Mayoral staff can be placed with an official. Lobbyists’ reports name 24 of the listed staff as the person contacted, 439 times in all. With a second link, 4 later appear as registered lobbyists contacting their old department, 1 at an organization that department funds, 12 came from the campaign of an official in the department that hired them, and 13 hold or held a board or commission seat under the same Form 700 account; 115 went on to another City department and 41 came from one. Lobbyists reported 2,377 contacts with 119 of these staff by name.
how: Staff are payroll names whose main job in a fiscal year is “Legislative Assistant” at the Board of Supervisors or “Mayoral Staff” in the Mayor’s department, under this project’s name rules (one spelling, never two full-time jobs at once). Moves to lobbying or to a funded organization are the rows of the people analysis for those two departments, and arrivals from a campaign are the rows of the jobs analysis; neither is recomputed here. A board or commission seat is shown only when the same Form 700 filer account lists it beside the staff position. An aide is “placed” with an official when the office’s own staff list names them (the Clerk’s Board Roster and each supervisor’s page, both of 2026; no earlier lists are published), when that official’s committee paid the same rare name as salary or consultant while both were in the department, or when a requested-payment filing names the aide as the official’s contact. For listed staff the row adds what the payroll, the official’s campaign payments and lobbyists’ reports show under the same name. Other moves between City departments are counted from the payroll and not named.
limits: Being connected is not being corrupt. Aides and Mayoral staff hold exempt appointments (the jobs analysis quotes the Charter rule); the City’s rules set one-year limits on leaving for advocacy, lobbying or a nonprofit, and none of the lobbying rows falls inside that year on the dates available. The payroll does not say which supervisor an aide works for, and staff lists exist only for 2026, so most past aides cannot be tied to an office. Being named in a lobbyist’s report means the aide took a meeting or a call, which is the job. Names are matched, not identities: every row carries its own match label. Staff before fiscal 2017 are not named in the payroll.
